In March 2010, the FDA revised the labeling for simvastatin and recommended that individuals of Chinese descent should not receive an 80 mg dose of simvastatin in combination with cholesterol-modifying doses of niacin-containing products. This recommendation was based on interim results from the Heart Protection Study. On June 8, 2011, the FDA issued an additional black box warning regarding the use of high-dose simvastatin. Following a review of data from the randomized clinical trial known as the Study of the Effectiveness of Additional Reductions in Cholesterol and Homocysteine (SEARCH), the FDA recommended limiting the use of high-dose simvastatin. The trial demonstrated a higher incidence of myopathy in patients treated with 80 mg of simvastatin compared to those receiving a 20 mg dose (9% in the intensive statin arm versus 0.03% in the standard dose arm). Recommendations: Simvastatin 80 mg should not be initiated in new patients, including those currently on lower doses of the medication. This dose should only be used in patients who have been taking it for more than 12 months without any evidence of myopathy. New contraindications and dose limitations were added to the labeling for use in combination with other medications.
